AgentPreview is display-only. ⚠ EVIDENCE LIVES IN CLOUD/EE: the `cloud @<sha>: packages/service-ai/...` paths cited below are the closed `@objectstack/service-ai` runtime in the CLOUD repo, NOT git-tracked framework code. 2026-08-30 (#13272): the previous wording of this sentence was false in BOTH halves. (a) It called the framework's own service-ai tree “a stale build artifact with no src/” — there is no tree at all: `packages/services/` holds every sibling service EXCEPT service-ai, and `git ls-files | grep -ic service-ai` returns 0. Absent, not stale. (b) The citations spelled `packages/services/service-ai/...`, a path present in NEITHER repo; cloud's real layout, measured at cloud@15f55df (#13042), is `packages/service-ai/...`. Every citation below now carries the explicit `cloud` realm marker, so it is attributed by the marker `scanEvidence` reads rather than riding the `FOREIGN_PATH_PREFIXES` special case that silently exempted the stale spelling from resolution — which is why 22 dead pointers sat green. ✅ RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-15 (#13272): the re-verification half this entry parked is discharged. Every cloud consumer cited below was re-read in a cloud checkout at cloud @cb8ee7ff60c097cc21a584fe9caf8ef4391cc0e8, and the ten rows the read confirmed now carry `verifiedAt`, `evidenceScope: cross-repo`, and a `#symbol` anchor pinned to the consumer instead of a line number — the two cited line numbers (`agent-runtime.ts:264`, `agent-access.ts:50`) had both drifted onto prose, which is the rot a line citation produces and a symbol does not. The anchors are the load-bearing half, and they are why the DATE matters: `scanEvidence` never collects an anchor while a foreign realm marker is in force, so CI cannot re-derive a single one of the cloud anchors — each rests on that dated reading alone. ⛔ Never re-stamp `verifiedAt` here without re-reading cloud; a bare re-stamp restores exactly the unfalsifiable pointer this entry's history is made of. ⛔ ONE ROW WAS DELIBERATELY NOT STAMPED, AND HAS SINCE BEEN RE-GRADED. `tools` was FALSIFIED by the same read: zero consumers in cloud at that ref, where the only two mentions are comments recording the removal of the branch, while this repo's own AgentSchema already declares the key `retiredKey(...)`. A `verifiedAt` beside `live` would have certified the wrong thing, so #13272 left that row's `status`, `note` and old evidence untouched and handed the liveness re-grade to triage as #18304; triage graded it (b) and the re-grade LANDED 2026-09-18 — `live` -> `dead`, the stale `evidence` pointer deleted, and the cloud reading attributed and dated inside the row's own `note`. Note the shape — that row sat `live` since the 2026-06 audit BECAUSE `FOREIGN_PATH_PREFIXES` exempted its citation from resolution, so the exemption this card was filed about had hidden a dead key, not only a misspelled path. These props are `live` because that cloud runtime consumes them; the OPEN framework edition does not — see content/docs/ai for the open/cloud boundary. 2026-07-30 (#3896 close-out sweep): the dead authoring keys were REMOVED — tombstoned at the schema with prescriptions (retiredKey) and stripped by the protocol-17 close-out conversions; entries deleted per the #3715 precedent. agent.knowledge (and AIKnowledgeSchema) removed; the topics→sources rename was absorbed into the removal pre-release.

tools.note: REMOVED in protocol 17 (#3894) — tombstoned at the schema (retiredKey carries the prescription; authoring it is a tsc error before any parse, and a parse error after) and dropped from legacy sources by the ADR-0087 conversion `agent-tools-to-skills`. The entry stays because retiredKey keeps the key in the walked shape (the rls.priority precedent); an agent reaches exactly the tools its surface-compatible skills declare (ADR-0064), so re-declare each entry in a skill — the `skills` row on this type is that slot. LEDGER CORRECTED 2026-09-18 (#18304) — the VERDICT moved `live` -> `dead`, a truth correction and not a relaxation: the row asserted `live` on a key this repo's own AgentSchema had tombstoned, which the published vocabulary cannot mean. `live` is defined as "Has a runtime consumer", and retiredKey types the key `never`, so no author can put a value behind it and no consumer in any repo can read one. THE LOAD-BEARING EVIDENCE IS LOCAL AND RE-MEASURABLE HERE, which is the half the old citation never had: the tombstone packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts#tools, the strip packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts#agentToolsToSkills — whose own docblock records that the cloud runtime stopped reading the field entirely (cloud#910) — and that conversion's D3 chain step in packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts. Both populations are covered without leaving this checkout: an authored source is refused at tsc and at parse, and a stored row or built artifact has the key DELETED by the replayed conversion chain at rehydration (ADR-0087 addendum, retired entries included) before any consumer sees it. The verdict is also read off this ledger's own convention rather than chosen: measured 2026-09-18 over the 36 governed types the gate walks, 40 top-level keys carry a `[REMOVED]` tombstone description and all 40 are never-typed — 39 of them said `dead` and this one said `live`, the single outlier in the class. ⚠ THE CROSS-REPO HALF IS NOT THIS SEAT'S READING. The zero-consumer census in cloud @cb8ee7ff60c097cc21a584fe9caf8ef4391cc0e8 (the only two mentions there are comments recording the branch's removal) and its lit positive control (`agent.skills`, four real reads in the same tree, same path shape) were taken by the #13272 re-verification on 2026-09-15 — the date stamped here, the same one its ten stamped siblings carry. Cloud is not reachable from an open-source checkout, so the seat that landed this correction re-derived the in-repo half only and cites the cloud half as attributed, never as its own measurement. `live-elsewhere` is REFUSED rather than undeclared: that status requires a genuine foreign enforcer, and a key nothing can carry a value for has nothing to enforce — the same read that would have to support it is the read that found zero. The old `evidence` string (`cloud: packages/service-ai/src/agent-runtime.ts`) is DELETED rather than repointed: a dead row's pointer lives in this note by the gate's own design (EVIDENCE_UNSCANNED_STATUSES in scripts/liveness/check-liveness.mts), and that string named the one file whose remaining mentions of the key are the comments recording its deletion. ⚠ WHY IT SAT `live` SINCE THE 2026-06 AUDIT — the row was exempt from scrutiny rather than scrutinised. Its citation spelled `packages/services/service-ai/...` until #13309, and `FOREIGN_PATH_PREFIXES` in scripts/liveness/evidence.mts classifies that prefix foreign and never resolves it; after the repoint the explicit `cloud` realm marker classifies it foreign too. Both spellings are unresolvable BY DESIGN, so no gate could fail on this row in either direction — only a human, or a seat with cloud access, ever could. NEXT STEP IS A SEPARATE CARD: with the row `dead`, the key is an ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove input (playbook `.claude/skills/spec-property-retirement`). ⛔ Not done here.
